source_section: the 53 unheld, uniquely-resolved wrong anchors - the 46 whose true id ESPN reports `completed: true` AND `STATUS_FINAL`
committed_by: lane1/409, scoped down to 46 by lane1/410 under CERT-3046; same attended protocol as populations 1 and 2
operation: UPDATE events.espn_id ONLY — correction, never deletion (ruling 079)
explicitly_not_written: home_score / away_score - 18 of these 46 rows ALREADY hold the correct final, so a repair that also 'tidied' the score would overwrite a correct final with another game's on 18 rows. Same refusal as population 2, measured again on this cohort.

commence_time - it is the ADDRESSED field here, never a written one. It equals the true game's start TO THE MINUTE on all 46 (delta 0.0 on every row), which is precisely what proves espn_id is the drifted field and not the time.

box_score_data - every row here carries one, and on a wrongly anchored row it was fetched for the wrong game. MEASURED on 2026-09-18, this is the reader-visible cost: on 27 of these 46 rows the stored inning-by-inning line score sums to the WRONG game's score, so the event page prints a final and a line score that contradict each other (ev12306380 shows 8-2 above a line adding to 1-7; ev12312422 shows 0-5 above 2-3). 18 agree and 1 has no line stored. It is still NOT rewritten here: `game_state_backfill` re-fetches it from `event.espn_id`, so correcting the id is what lets the owning writer replace it. A repair that wrote the payload itself would be forging an observation.
no deletion of any row, under any branch (ruling 079)
why_this_file_is_committed: The reviewed object is a SET OF TRIPLES, not a count — an approval given over a number
does not transfer to whatever a later re-derivation finds under that number.
Every row here was cross-checked TWICE against ESPN, independently of the repair
rail's own computation and independently of the stored espn_id. First by the deriving
pass: a scoreboard sweep of 192 ET dates, 3/19-9/26, 2,522 fixtures, which is a
DEREFERENCE of each stored id and not a model of it (an id-vs-date curve screen was
built first and measured at ~10% precision / 40% recall, and is recorded as a negative
result rather than used). Second by an independent /summary read of all 53 targets,
asserting per row: the true game's start equals our commence_time to the minute, both
team names match in the correct home/away orientation, and ESPN state is FINAL.
Result: 50 AGREE, 3 REJECT - and that AGREE count was WRONG BY FOUR; see the POSTPONED block below, which is why the set here is 46.
The defect is legible in the rows themselves: on every one of the 46, the WRONG id is
an earlier meeting of the SAME series between the SAME two clubs — `wrong_id_is` and
`true_id_is` are printed side by side so a reviewer can see that without a tool.
THREE rows were examined and are deliberately ABSENT, and two of them are close calls
stated plainly rather than quietly rounded in:
12828738 (true 401814817) and 13362745 (true 401814863) match on teams, on FINAL,
and on the exact score, and miss the to-the-minute test by ONE minute (we store
:21 and :06, ESPN says :20 and :05). They are almost certainly correct. They are
out because this population's admission test is 'proven', not 'probably', and a
write rail is the wrong place to spend a precedent for loosening it; admitting them
is a population 4 with its own review, not an edit to this file.
15185681 has a commence_time 240 minutes off and a stored score matching no game
within three days. Population 2's reviewed set named this same row as deliberately
absent for the same reason on 2026-08-20; this pass reached that verdict again
independently, which is the cross-check working.
Also OUT OF THIS POPULATION, by construction and not by omission:
11 rows whose correct id is ALREADY HELD by a second events row. Those are twins,
and 10 of the 11 pairs render two different final scores for one game. The holder
must be folded BEFORE the loser can be re-stamped, so they are a fold ship, not a
re-stamp ship, and the rail's own true_id_holders gate would refuse them anyway.
5 doubleheader rows whose date+pair resolves to TWO ESPN ids, so which meeting the
row means is not decidable from the anchor alone. Population 2 excluded its three
doubleheaders for this reason; this follows that precedent.
FOUR MORE ROWS WERE REMOVED AFTER REVIEW, and the reason is a defect in this file's own
second cross-check rather than anything about the rows:
(401815904) each dereference live as STATUS_POSTPONED, `completed: false`, 0-0. The
verifying pass defined final as ESPN `state == 'post'`, AND ESPN USES 'post' FOR
POSTPONED AS WELL AS FOR FINAL, so all four were classified AGREE by a predicate that
could not tell the two apart. The committed rows even printed the word Postponed in
their own `true_id_is` text.
They are a CLASS, not four accidents: a postponed original keeps its id and the make-up
game is played under a DIFFERENT one, so our row - which carries a real final from the
make-up - can never be anchored to the shell. The make-up id is not derivable from the
sweep that found these (it looked at the original date), so the correct id is unknown and
these rows stay wrongly anchored until a pass that asks for it. Re-stamping them would
have pointed four completed rows at an authority record that says no game was played.
Found by CERT-3046. The predicate is now `completed is True` AND `STATUS_FINAL`, all 46
survivors were re-checked under it (46 STRICT_FINAL, 0 NOT_FINAL), and
`test_no_reviewed_row_names_a_non_final_game` guards every population against the class.
